title: Content Brief
description: The shared decision about which content to make, written before any draft, prompt, or script exists. It is an input contract rather than a skill's own output: draft-evidence-content and osmu-fanout both read it, so the topic is fixed once and every downstream surface inherits the same audience, question, and evidence scope. A brief is not append-only history; it is a plan file that is rewritten until the person owning it stops changing it.

owner.description: The person accountable for the topic choice. Choosing what to publish is a promise to customers, so it is not delegated to the model.

audience.description: Who this is for, stated concretely enough that a reader can tell whether they are excluded.

question.description: The single reader question the content answers.

intent.description: Why the reader arrives. It decides the CTA boundary, not the writing style.

source_signal_ids.description: Triaged customer signals that made this topic worth writing about.

source_observation_ids.description: Answer-surface observations that made this topic worth writing about.

evidence_ids.description: The evidence the draft may cite. Evidence outside this list is out of scope for this brief.

planned_outputs.description: Which surfaces this one brief will be reused for. Naming them here is what makes the surfaces reuse a single decision instead of drifting into three different topics.

limitations.description: What this brief's evidence cannot support. Required, because a brief with no stated limit reads as unlimited.

cta.description: The next step offered to the reader, or null when no landing point is validated yet. Null is a decision, not a missing field.

publication_boundary.description: What this brief does not authorize. Publishing, sending, and deploying stay outside every skill that reads the brief.

allOf.description: A topic must name where it came from. At least one triaged signal or one visibility observation is required, so no content is planned from an unrecorded hunch.
A brief that plans a blog draft must name the evidence that draft may cite, because draft-evidence-content builds its claim ledger from this scope.
